content:
kevin: Heads-up — noticed a sharp tail-latency jump from the continuous-batcher this afternoon for model semislim-7b (hosted pool). 95p went ~120ms -> ~480ms in ~6m, throughput steady but many microbatches elongated. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/team/eng-runtime/boards/continuous-batcher

anya: thanks, do we have a correlation with kernel selector flips or KV cache churn?

kevin: initial traces point to kernel-selector choosing a slower kernel for medium-length sequences around 256 tokens after a batch-shift. Also seeing KV cache eviction spikes on a subset of shards.

perf-bot: alert: continuous-batcher.tail_latency.p95 increased to 480ms at 2024-07-11T15:12:30Z (baseline 130ms).

sophie: can someone paste profiler snapshot? hope it's not the recent kernel-intro change.

kevin: dropping snippets: 
```
# top of timeline from flamegraph (condensed)
continuous_batcher::admit -> packer::repack -> kernel_selector::choose(slow-path)
runtime::kv_cache::evict(major) x45
gpu_op::fused_attention(slow_kernel)  — 36% extra cycles
```

marcus: hmm kv evictions + slow kernel selection could be a feedback loop: smaller microbatches cause different sequence-length distribution, kernel selector mis-estimates perf -> picks conservative kernel -> increases processing time -> batching window grows -> more microbatching.

anya: can we repro in staging with the same tenant-mix? maybe a noisy tenant pushed prefix-heavy requests.

kevin: started a staging replay with traffic trace id tf-replay-20240711-15. Replaying now with kvcache disabled to isolate.

deploy-bot: replay job tf-replay-20240711-15 started on staging-cluster-rw1 (job id r-20240711-77).

perf-bot: staging run summary (first 10m): p95 140ms (kvcache off), p99 360ms. With kvcache on it's p95 470ms, p99 900ms.

sophie: that points at KV cache interaction. any recent changes to eviction thresholds or bloom filter heuristics?

marcus: yes, we recently increased kvcache.max_entries_per_shard by 15% to reduce cold misses for embeddings workloads. Might be causing larger compaction stalls under churn.

anya: idea: temporarily revert the max_entries bump in hosting-pool config and restart batcher on a small canary pool. If latency normalizes we know it's the eviction/compaction path.

kevin: rolling revert to canary now (canary id cb-canary-12). Will monitor.

perf-bot: canary metrics: before revert p95=460ms, after revert (2m) p95=135ms.

kevin: looks like a compaction/eviction tail. We'll keep canary reverted and open a JIRA to investigate compaction GC path + kernel selector heuristics.

anya: assign to eng-runtime/kevin + eng-runtime/marcus. Add perf/regressions label and include the replay trace and profiler output.

kevin: created RW-1234 with logs + flamegraph + replay link. Planning next: 1) root-cause compaction pause, 2) tune eviction thresholds, 3) adjust kernel-selector scoring to be less sensitive to transient length shifts.

marcus: also add an experiment to bias kernel-selector toward faster kernels for small microbatch sizes — might avoid the flip loop.

kevin: agreed. I'll post a short postmortem draft once we have full profiling. Thanks :thumbsup:

sophie: nice catch everyone.
